name: Canada
eligibility: The federal sources verified for this page govern reimbursement rather than who may commission a surrogacy, so no eligibility statement is made here.
paymentModel: Reimbursement only. Under the Assisted Human Reproduction Act regulations, expenditures incurred by a surrogate mother in relation to her surrogacy may be reimbursed. Regulated reimbursement is permitted; paying a person to act as a surrogate is not. Health Canada's guidance enumerates reimbursable costs, requires receipts, and requires records to be kept for five years.
parentage: Parentage after birth is a matter of provincial and territorial law. The federal sources checked here do not set it, and this page makes no claim about it.

facts.claim: Expenditures incurred by a surrogate mother in relation to her surrogacy may be reimbursed under subsection 12(1) of the Assisted Human Reproduction Act.

source.label: Assisted Human Reproduction (Reimbursement of Expenditures) Regulations, SOR-2019-193
source.supports: The regulation itself, registered 10 June 2019 and in force 9 June 2020. This is statutory text rather than a commentary on it.

facts.claim: Reimbursable surrogate costs enumerated by the regulator include travel, childcare, counselling, legal fees, medications, maternity clothing, prenatal classes, delivery, insurance, and lost work-related income during the pre-pregnancy and post-partum period, with receipts required and records kept for five years.

source.label: Reimbursement of expenditures incurred by a surrogate applicant or a surrogate in relation to her surrogacy (consultation document)
source.supports: Government guidance published alongside the regulations, which states that the regulations take effect on 9 June 2020. Guidance documents describe the regulator's expectations; the regulation text governs.

openQuestions: Which province or territory you give birth in or take the child home to changes the parentage answer. Provincial rules were not verified for this page.
The line between permitted reimbursement and a prohibited payment turns on the specifics of an arrangement. That is a question for a Canadian lawyer, not something a reimbursement list settles.
Whether a child born abroad through surrogacy can be registered or enter Canada involves federal and provincial rules beyond the sources recorded here.
